title: Honest Inference for Variance-Weighted Dose-Response Summaries with Non-Gaussian Outcomes
banked_reason: kernel_substituted@thm:certified-loose-frontiers: sound nonmatching brackets replace the promised matched risk, honest-length, and adaptation kernel, which remains open; independent validity gate confirms no bounded same-topic repair.

The theorem’s justification does not make a precise theorem-level comparison with the closest Liu and Robins result classes, so the note does not yet establish why these particular loose original-law brackets are a new contribution rather than an application of existing nonlinear-functional machinery.
proof_attempt_summary: One D0 solver round delivered nonmatching risk and parent-honest interval-length brackets, an explicit interval and affine root-n sufficiency; the informal math panel passed. D0.5 decision review rejected substitution of that partial theorem for the promised matched risk/length/adaptation kernel; an independent main validity consult confirmed no bounded faithful repair. The multiresolution contraction ladder, coupled-mixture converse, affine-null comparison and smallest adaptation price remain open. No F stages ran and no Lean certification was produced.
tldr: Continuous-dose summaries can use an outcome-variance-dependent weight to emphasize precise parts of the response curve. In a known-uniform-dose benchmark with arbitrary conditional outcome shape, we prove root-sample-size minimax risk on the affine slice, construct a total original-data interval with finite-sample coverage over the entire parent, and certify explicit lower and upper bounds for slice risk, parent-honest expected length, and simultaneous adaptation. Writing \(d=\min\{\delta,1\}\), \(r=4\beta/(1+4\beta)\), and \(s_\beta=\beta/(1+2\beta)\), the certified risk and length lower bounds are of order \(n^{-1/2}+dn^{-r}\), while the attained upper bounds are respectively \(n^{-1/2}+dn^{-s_\beta}\) and \(n^{-1/2}+(d+n^{-4/9})n^{-s_\beta}\). The interval has affine-slice root-sample-size expected length for \(\beta\ge1/16\). Matching the local exponents, determining necessity of the honest affine boundary, and identifying the exact adaptation price remain open.
gap: General nonlinear-functional estimation does not, through the inspected theorem statements, evaluate this learned reciprocal-variance ratio on shrinking affine-residual slices or give its parent-honest length benchmark.
fill: The complete original-law risk, honest-length, and adaptation orders must be derived together, with total observable attainment and legal same-class converses. Fixed-curvature rates, a target gradient, and Gaussian special cases alone do not satisfy the kernel.
